messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a 4-region microbench (us-west1 / eu-west1 / asia-east1 / us-east1) comparing L4 vs T4 vs A10G for embeddings + small-chat (<=128 tokens). Unexpected A10G behavior in eu-west that looks kernel-related. Posting short summary + logs, pls chime in.

maria: command we used:
```
./bench --model small-chat-v1 --modes embed,chat --regions us-west1,eu-west1,asia-east1,us-east1 --gpus L4,T4,A10G --qps 200 --dur 5m --seq 128
```

maria: summary (p50 latency / throughput per GPU / cost per 1M tokens approximated):
- Embeddings:
  - L4: 12ms / 1400 qps / $0.28
  - T4: 45ms / 420 qps / $0.11
  - A10G: 20ms / 900 qps / $0.35
- Small-chat (avg 80 tokens):
  - L4: 18ms p50 / 1100 tok/s / $0.32
  - T4: 60ms / 340 tok/s / $0.12
  - A10G: 26ms / 760 tok/s / $0.38

maria: notable anomaly: eu-west1 A10G chat p50 jumped to ~90ms during a 20min window (whole-run p50 for eu-west1 A10G = 62ms vs other regions 26ms). Kernel selection logs show repeated picks of `int8_gemm_kernel_v2` and a fallback loop: "selected kernel int8_gemm_kernel_v2 -> perf counter spike -> fallback int8_gemm_kernel_v1 -> fallback_fp16=false"

josh: Hmm. sounds like kernel-selector oscillation. we've seen int8 kernels be flaky on A10G with driver X.Y.Z. Did you capture per-evict logs?

maria: yes attached snippet from runtime.log (copied below).
```
[12:03:15] kernel-selector: chosen=int8_gemm_kernel_v2 score=87
[12:03:15] perf-monitor: l2-miss spike -> 2x latency spike
[12:03:15] kernel-selector: fallback to int8_gemm_kernel_v1
[12:03:16] kernel-selector: chosen=int8_gemm_kernel_v2 score=85
[12:03:16] perf-monitor: spike persists
[12:03:17] runtime: forced-policy=auto, fallback_fp16=false
```

priya: quick quality note: we did an embeddings drift check after quantizing to 8-bit (per-candidate symmetric). cosine similarity drop ~0.7% median, 99th ~1.9%. For small-chat with 8-bit enabled we saw a tiny uptick in hallucination tokens on long-tail prompts (~1.2% regression on our eval set). For embeddings workload that trade is fine in many ad-hoc retrieval flows but flagging it.

josh: on the kernel side: A10G silicon + our nv driver apparently prefers int8 path for perf. If perf-monitor oscillates (L2/cache), we get jitter. short-term workaround: set env KERNEL_PRIORITY=fp16 or KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fp16 for canary nodes. Also bump kernel-stability threshold in selector to avoid flip-flopping.

alex: for capacity planning numbers (steady-state per-GPU realistic QPS we measured):
- embeddings: L4 ~1300 qps, T4 ~400 qps, A10G ~850 qps
- small-chat (80 tokens): L4 ~1000 tok/s, T4 ~320 tok/s, A10G ~720 tok/s
recommendation: plan with 20% headroom + 1.25x peak multiplier. autoscale target GPU util = 60-65% for tail latency safety.

alex: cost-per-1M-tokens rough calc we used above assumes instance cost + normalized token work; numbers are approximate for sizing conversations and TCO comparisons (use Optimize for precise).

infra-bot: note: eu-west1 A10G host images on that pool are using driver 525.85, runtime 2.7.0. us-west1 and us-east1 are on 526.x + runtime 2.8.0. difference could explain kernel scoring.

deploy-bot: canary suggestion: enable KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fp16 on 2 A10G nodes in eu-west1 for 1 hour during traffic window, observe p50/p95 and perf-monitor. I can spin up the canary if you tag the pool. :gear:

priya: one more thing on quant: If we use mixed strategy (embeds=8bit, chat=fp16) we keep embed unit economics but avoid chat regressions. For customers that only use embeddings, L4 still wins on latency/cost for small vectors; A10G is good if you need model size > 20B or higher throughput density per rack.

josh: longer-term fix: tweak kernel-selector to use stability-weighted scoring (score -= volatility_penalty). I can prototype a quick patch that adds a 5-10% penalty to kernels that triggered >2 fallbacks in last minute.

maria: next steps I propose:
- @deploy-bot spin the fp16 canary on 2 A10G eu-west1 nodes (deploy-bot: ack)
- @josh prototype selector volatility penalty (small PR)
- @priya run a 24h embed-only quant sweep to map drift distribution across datasets
- @alex update sizing doc with the numbers above and recommended autoscale defaults

maria: thanks all — will post canary results & raw bench logs here once ready. :thumbsup:
